entry.hook: Jin Dasheng (a horse yao who could outrun any pursuer but never outran heaven's judgment) was the fastest among the Seven Monsters of Mount Mei—and the first to die trying to escape. His hooves beat the earth like thunder, yet they could not carry him past a single celestial blade.

body.body_1:
Jin Dasheng / 金大升  
Original Form: Horse (马)  
Birth Era: Late Shang Dynasty, during the Investiture of the Gods  
Shapeshifted Form: Human male form achieved, retains horse-like speed and a mane of coarse hair.
body.body_2:
Current Realm: Jie Dan (Core Formation).  
Cultivation Duration: Centuries, from awakening to his death on the battlefield.  
Bottleneck: He never advanced beyond core formation. Without the Xian Tian Dao Ti and lacking any divine inheritance, he relied solely on raw physical speed and strength. His failure to master any defensive or evasive magic meant that when faced with a celestial opponent, he had no recourse but flight—and even that failed him.
body.body_3: Qi Zhi (Awakening): The tradition states that Jin Dasheng was a horse grazing on the slopes of Mount Mei when he accidently swallowed a spirit herb. That night, for the first time, he saw the moon and understood it was round and cold. He looked at his own hooves and knew he would one day die. The herd sensed something alien in him and drove him away. He spent years wandering alone, speaking to the wind. His awakening was not a blessing but an exile: he could think, but no one could hear him.
body.body_4: Jie Dan (Core Formation): Without human meridians, he forced the wild energy of sun and moon into his abdomen by sheer will. Lunar essence froze his intestines; solar essence scorched them. The two clashed inside him like warring armies. The Yao Dan that formed was a crude, unstable mass—always pulsing, always threatening to detonate. He learned to live with the pain, but every gallop sent waves of internal fire through his gut.
body.body_5: Hua Xing (Shapeshifting): He spent decades re-forming his equine skeleton into a human shape. It was a slow, conscious surgery: breaking each leg bone, reshaping the spine, compressing the ribcage. The Shapeshifting Thunder Tribulation struck as he emerged from a cave on Mount Mei—three bolts that scarred his back with lightning burns he never healed. His human form was broad and muscular, but he kept a rough mane down his neck and his hooves never fully turned into human feet: they remained hardened, cloven, always making a sharp click when he walked.
body.body_6: Fan Zu (Bloodline Atavism): Not recorded. His blood carried no known ancient beast. He remained a simple horse yao, with no ancestral will to fight and no primordial power to awaken. In this, he was both fortunate and limited: no risk of Duo She, but also no hidden reserve to draw upon when needed.
body.body_7: Core Obsession: The only thing that kept him going was the love of the open plain—the feeling of wind against his mane, the pounding rhythm of hooves on earth. He had no great ambition, no desire to conquer or prove himself. He simply wanted to run forever, unbound. His tragedy is that even this modest wish was denied. In the most common reading, when the Shang dynasty summoned the Seven Monsters, he joined out of loyalty to his sworn brother Yuan Hong, not out of any personal agenda. On the battlefield, when he saw that he could not win, his instinct was to flee—to find any open plain where he could disappear. But the plain was already gone.
body.body_8:
- With the immortal path: Killed by Yang Jian (Erlang Shen), a celestial warrior of formidable power. There was no prolonged duel; Yang Jian's divine spells bypassed Jin Dasheng's speed entirely.  
- With the divine path: After death, his soul was taken to the Fengshen Platform and enfeoffed as Daluan Xing (Star of Great Calamity), a minor star divinity governing sudden disasters.  
- With mortals: No direct records of interaction.  
- With the yao path: He was the youngest of the Seven Monsters of Mount Mei, bound to Yuan Hong and his other brothers by oath. He was known among them as the swiftest and the most straightforward—a brother who trusted in speed and loyalty.
body.body_9:
Current Situation: His spirit resides in the celestial office of the Star of Great Calamity, a low-ranking divine appointment that carries no real power or respect.  
Probable End: He has already reached his end. There is no further cultivation, no return to the mortal realm.  
Legacy: Among later yao, his name is repeated as a caution—a reminder that raw speed is not enough, and that loyalty to a doomed cause can cost you everything. He left no teachings, no secret method, only a hoofprint in the cosmic ledger.
body.body_11: The entry for Jin Dasheng belongs to the lore of the Seven Monsters of Mount Mei, a brotherhood of yao who fought on the Shang side during the Investiture of the Gods. His fall at the hands of Yang Jian marks a turning point in that campaign. Within the broader yao tradition, he is often read as a figure of tragic simplicity—a creature of pure instinct who never learned to cheat death through guile or magic. His enfeoffment as a minor disaster star places him within the celestial bureaucracy created by the Fengshen system, linking him to other fallen yao divinities.

guide.guide_1: Imagine a horse. Not just any horse—one that one night stops grazing, looks up at the moon, and suddenly understands: *that thing up there is round, and cold, and I will never touch it. And one day I will stop breathing.* That is the awakening of a yao. Jin Dasheng was that horse. He stood on a mountainside, trembling, while the rest of the herd fled from him because he smelled wrong. He had no one to tell. That night, he began his long, lonely walk out of the meadow and into a world that would never accept him.
guide.guide_2: If you've ever skimmed the *Investiture of the Gods*, you might remember a string of monster names—Meishan Seven Monsters, all of them cannon fodder for the heroes. Jin Dasheng is the horse one. Usually he's just a speed bump. But if you stop and look closer, you see a creature who traded his freedom for brotherhood and paid with his life. The stories leave out the cost: the decades of pain to become human, the lightning scars, the desperate attempt to run away in the end. Let me tell you the version nobody talks about.
guide.guide_3: You know Kafka's *Metamorphosis*? A man wakes up as an insect. That's the Western nightmare. Jin Dasheng's nightmare was the opposite: a horse woke up as a *self*. He could think, remember, fear death—but he was still a horse. No one else in the herd had his problem. They just ate and slept and foaled. He watched them and felt an unbearable loneliness. It's like being the only person in the world who suddenly realizes you're going to die, and everyone else is still dancing. He tried to join them, but his own kind shunned him. He tried to join humans, but they shot arrows at him. There was nowhere to go.
guide.guide_4: Let me lay out the price tag. To form his Yao Dan, he swallowed lunar essence—you know, like swallowing liquid nitrogen—and solar essence—like swallowing a hot coal. Then he let them fight inside him until a lump of unstable energy formed. He bled from the mouth for weeks. To shapeshift, he broke every bone in his body, one by one, and rearranged them into a human frame. No anesthesia. The Thunder Tribulation hit him three times, leaving permanent burn scars on his spine. And after all that, what did he get? A body that could run fast but had zero defense against magic. It's like a Faustian bargain, except there's no Mephistopheles to complain to. The universe just takes your labor and gives you a crippled tool.
guide.guide_5: Why did he stay and fight for the Shang? Most readers assume he was evil or greedy. But the simplest reading is: his sworn brother Yuan Hong asked him. Yuan Hong had saved his life once, and loyalty meant something to this creature who had no other family. When the battle turned, he didn't want to die for a fallen dynasty—he wanted to live for the next gallop across an open field. But by then there was no field left. He turned to run, and Yang Jian's blade caught him. He wasn't a hero or a villain. He was just a horse that had learned to stand on two legs, and he still couldn't outrun fate.
guide.guide_6: The Seven Monsters of Mount Mei were brothers by oath—Yuan Hong the Bull, Zhu Zizhen the Gingall, Chang Hao the Snake, and so on. Jin Dasheng was the youngest, the fastest, the one who laughed loudest. They trusted each other. But when the celestial army came, that trust broke one by one. Yang Jian didn't duel Jin Dasheng; he used divine tricks—the dog, the magic fan. Jin Dasheng had no answer except to run. And in the end, he ran alone. If you were him, after centuries of solitude, after trusting only your brothers, and then losing them one by one—would you ever bet on anyone again? Probably not.
guide.guide_7: Jin Dasheng's story is small. He didn't change the world. He didn't leave a school of cultivation. But he reminds us of something universal: the desire to just *run*—to feel the wind in your hair and forget everything else. That desire is pure, and the world has a way of crushing pure things. In the end, he became a star—a minor one, governing calamities. It's an ironic reward for a creature who only wanted peace. But maybe that's the point. Every yao's struggle is a mirror for everyone who has ever felt out of place. The horse that woke up and found himself alone in a world that would never see him as anything but an animal. That horse is a little bit in all of us.

seo.meta_description: Jin Dasheng, one of the Seven Monsters of Mount Mei, was a horse yao of unmatched speed whose devotion to his brothers led to his death at the hands of Yang Jian. His tragedy lies in the gap between raw instinct and celestial power.
seo.og_title: Jin Dasheng: The Horse Yao Who Could Not Outrun Heaven
seo.og_description: Sworn brother of the Seven Monsters, faster than any pursuer, yet helpless before divine magic. His story is the quiet tragedy of a creature who only wanted the open plain.
seo.twitter_title: Jin Dasheng (金大升) – Horse Yao of the Meishan Seven
seo.twitter_description: The fastest yao on the battlefield, the first to fall. A story of loyalty, loneliness, and the cost of being born as a beast in a world that values gods.

lore_entries.description: A brotherhood of seven yao cultivators who gathered on Mount Mei during the Shang Dynasty, each with a distinct animal origin. Led by Yuan Hong.
A powerful celestial warrior and nephew of the Jade Emperor, known for his third eye and divine dog. A key adversary of the Meishan yao.
Star of Great Calamity, a minor celestial office governing sudden disasters such as plagues, landslides, and shipwrecks.
The celestial platform where souls of fallen warriors and yao were enfeoffed as star deities during the Investiture of the Gods.

faq_entries.question: Why was Jin Dasheng killed so easily if he was so fast?
faq_entries.answer: His speed was physical, not magical. Yang Jian used divine spells and his celestial dog to bypass Jin Dasheng's natural advantage, leaving the horse yao with no counter.

faq_entries.question: What is the Star of Great Calamity?
faq_entries.answer: A low-ranking star office in the celestial bureaucracy established by the Fengshen system, governing sudden disasters. Jin Dasheng was assigned this role after death.

faq_entries.question: How did Jin Dasheng awaken as a yao?
faq_entries.answer: He accidentally swallowed a spirit herb while grazing on Mount Mei. This triggered sentience, causing him to perceive the moon, mortality, and his own isolation.
